body.statement: Can one construct parameter-independent Markov kernels between the exact Gaussian block-mean and residual-scatter experiment generated by the observed panel and \(Z\sim N(u,I(\theta_0)^{-1})\) whose deficiencies vanish uniformly for \(u\in\mathcal U\), while simultaneously transporting the bounded curve-diameter loss, repairing vanishing coverage deficits, and preserving \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U,t\in\mathcal D}|\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)|\to0\)?
body.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step: LAN weak convergence alone does not transfer simultaneous coverage and worst-case expected maximum width for arbitrary randomized bands.
body.gap: LeCamYang2000 gives experiment-comparison tools, but no located result supplies this compact-local Gaussian--Wishart transfer for a moving-KKT curve target and a discontinuous coverage constraint.
body.consumer: Closing the transfer makes the computed Gaussian benchmark a sharp statement about procedures using the actual partially observed panel.
